rule:
Exact deterministic per-body resting postures with barrier-based classes (19 Nov 2026; Cormac: "the problem is that the
precomputation is random. it must be deterministic"). Same height function h(g) = sigma_K(g) - c.g and minima as exact_v1.py
(see its docstring); v1 grouped minima by angle, which chains the mug's facets and tilted postures together. v2 groups them by the
physical barrier: the rise of the centre of mass needed to roll alone from one resting posture to another.
  merge tree   sublevel sets of h on the Fibonacci lattice graph (k nearest neighbours): edges weighted max(h_p, h_q), processed in
               ascending order (minimum spanning tree), union-find; when two basins meet at height w the one with the higher minimum
               dies with persistence w - h(its minimum) = the least COM rise that rolls it into the other basin (elder rule).
  coarse       persistence-based clustering (ToMATo, Chazal et al. 2013): a basin is merged into its neighbour iff its persistence
               < tau; tau = middle of the largest gap in the sorted persistences (0 prepended).
  fine         refined exact minima (Nelder-Mead in a tangent chart from every lattice minimum), merged within the 1 mm rest-tolerance
               angle; each takes the coarse class of its lattice point. Lattice spacing ~0.3 deg at M = 400000.
Also writes lattice.npz (lattice directions with their coarse class and descent minimum) so a scene body can be given the class
of the basin it would roll into alone. Deterministic: no random numbers, no simulation.
v3 (19 Nov): fine postures are only refined minima that are strict local minima on a ring at the rest-tolerance angle (the floor);
a lattice minimum whose refinement drifts more than 2 degrees is a discretisation artefact on a slope and is dropped (v2 kept such
lattice points, which gave the spoon hundreds of spurious postures). Coarse classes (merge tree, ToMATo) unchanged.
usage: exact_v3.py OUTDIR [--M 400000] [--k 10]
model: model_rigidcontact.xml (MuJoCo model of the research code; primitives in primitives.json)
